record.file_problem: The post's text is present, but equations and figures are missing or do not render in the supplied text.
record.tranche_reason: It quantifies cosine interference among feature vectors and discusses superposition, but does not measure neuron responses or whether neurons have polysemantic jobs.
record.gate_note: The reported results concern geometric overlap among vectors, not the claim's neuron-level behavior. The results are recorded under fits_no_version. The post also cites the Toy Models of Superposition work; cited results are not recorded as this post's findings.
record.test_reason: The post computes geometric overlap (mean max absolute cosine similarity) among random or synthetic concept vectors. It does not measure neuron responses, the share of polysemantic neurons, or whether packing features causes polysemantic neurons in trained networks. It neither tests nor uses the claim's neuron-level finding.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that random directions in high dimensions are already near-optimal. They also conclude that 16k features in 768 dims give more interference than trillions of features in 4k+ dims. On that basis SynthSAEBench-16k has enough superposition to be realistic. The post makes no claim about neuron polysemanticity.
record.recipe_differences: The post uses geometric calculations and random-vector simulations, rather than a neuron-response measurement.

fits_no_version.finding: For random unit vectors, the expected mean max absolute cosine similarity matches simulation. Interference grows slowly with vector count and falls with dimension: 10^13 vectors in 8192 dims show less interference than 100K in 768 dims. Optimal placement barely improves on random placement.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In high-dimensional spaces, random feature directions are near-optimally spread by worst-case cosine interference, so very many features fit with low overlap.

fits_no_version.finding: SynthSAEBench-16k (16k directions, 768 dims) has MMACS 0.14. The post says this is roughly equal to 1B random vectors in 2048 dims.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The synthetic SAE benchmark's designed feature geometry has more interference than plausible real-LLM feature counts at large hidden sizes.

record.problems: The supplied text omits mathematical expressions and figures, so specific formula details and some numerical comparisons cannot be checked here. The geometric results do not establish neuron-level polysemanticity or a causal link between feature packing and mixed neuron responses.

untested.parts: It is assumed in the framing that models use superposition. There is no measurement of trained networks' feature counts or of neuron polysemanticity.

record.verdict_notes: All results are geometric calculations or simulations on random vectors, plus one designed synthetic model. There is no neuron-level measurement. The post assumes superposition (it cites Toy Models) rather than testing it. It is not an original source.

versions.untested_parts: The post measures vector overlap, not whether trained networks represent more sparse features than neurons or whether that causes polysemantic neurons.
